That said, I'll believe the "unprecedented scale" claims when I see them actually deployed in a real enterprise environment, not just in a pitch deck.

ai-at-work.excerpt: Researchers at artificial intelligence security company Noma Security Inc. today disclosed a critical prompt injection vulnerability in GitHub Inc.’s new Agentic Workflows feature that allowed an unau
ai-at-work.dwp_take: GitHub's new AI workflow feature had a critical flaw that let attackers steal private code by posting a rigged issue in a public repository, which GitHub has now patched. This matters because many organizations are rushing AI tools into their dev workflows without thinking through the security implications, and this is exactly the kind of mess that happens when speed beats caution. After three decades watching tech teams, I'll say it plain: just because your shiny new AI can do something doesn't mean it should do it unsupervised with access to your crown jewels.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Picus Security bundled breach simulation, penetration testing, and exposure validation into one automated platform so security teams can answer faster whether a new vulnerability actually threatens their environment. This matters because digital workplace pros are tired of security theater where vulnerabilities get flagged but nobody knows if they're real problems or false alarms. Finally, a tool that lets security teams stop playing guessing games and start giving straight answers to the one question that actually keeps executives awake at night.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Assail released Sidewinder, an AI security tool that can identify vulnerabilities and fix them automatically without waiting for human approval. That said, I've seen plenty of "self-fixing" systems create new problems faster than they solve old ones, so let's see if this one actually works before we pop the champagne.

tools-tech.dwp_take: ZDNet tested three wireless charging stands with cooling technology to see which one actually prevents heat buildup during charging. tools-tech.title: Talk, talk, talk: The rise of AI dictation tools at work

tools-tech.dwp_take: AI dictation tools are becoming standard issue for knowledge workers drowning in typing, particularly those heavy users hammering out prompts to AI assistants all day. Here's the thing though: we've been promised voice-to-text salvation for twenty years, and it keeps flopping until the underlying tech actually gets good, so let's pump the brakes on declaring this the end of the keyboard before we see real adoption numbers.

digital-culture.title: Are managers becoming obsolete—or more important than ever?
digital-culture.excerpt: The rise of artificial intelligence and shifting workplace dynamics like flatter organizational structures have sparked intense debate about the future role of managers. Eight industry experts weigh i
digital-culture.dwp_take: Managers are caught in that classic corporate squeeze where AI is doing their analysis work while flatter structures strip away their authority, leaving everyone arguing about whether they're headed for extinction or evolution. This matters because your organization's entire communication strategy, knowledge management system, and employee engagement programs all collapse without clarity on what managers actually do anymore. Here's the thing though: managers aren't becoming obsolete, they're just finally being forced to justify their existence beyond scheduling meetings and approving timesheets.
